title: Volunteer Monitors and HF operating
blurb: Explain the Volunteer Monitor Program, aim long-path beams, call CQ on HF, and know logs, contest ID and QRP.

G2D01.why: Volunteer Monitors are amateurs **formally enlisted to monitor the airwaves for rules violations**.
G2D01.trap: Exams, coordination and civil defense are other volunteer jobs.

G2D02.why: The program aims to **encourage self-regulation and compliance** with the rules.

G2D03.why: Monitors **compare beam headings** on the repeater input from different homes. The headings cross at the source.

G2D04.why: An azimuthal map centred on you shows **true bearings and distances** from that one location.
G2D04.trap: It doesn't show accurate land masses, and it isn't a satellite map.

G2D05.why: A general call is **"CQ" a few times, "this is", your call a few times, then pause** and listen. Repeat as needed.
G2D05.trap: QTC relates to traffic, and a bare carrier tells nobody who you are.

G2D06.why: The long path is the other way round the Earth, so aim **180° from the short-path heading**.

G2D07.why: The **NATO phonetic alphabet** runs Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta. The others are different alphabets.

G2D08.why: A log **helps you reply if the FCC asks about your station**. It isn't required for renewal or DX contacts.

G2D09.why: In a contest you must still **identify per the normal FCC rules**. Logs and QSL cards are not FCC requirements.

G2D11.why: Reports let each station **adjust to conditions**, such as power, speed or mode.
